start.text: A detective. I wondered when someone quieter than the constables might show up. I can't speak freely — I have clients.

choices.text: You were at the manor Thursday night.
Tell me about your relationship with Lady Harrington.
You're frightened of something.
I'll come back when you're ready to talk.

manor_thursday.text: I visit the manor regularly. It is a professional relationship. I have already told the constables this.

choices.text: You were there the night he died.
What did you discuss on those visits?
You're frightened.

night_press.text: I — yes. I was there. She asked me to come. To witness a document.

choices.text: She. Lady Harrington asked you?
What document?

lady_h_named.text: I have said too much already. If she hears I've been talking...

choices.text: She threatened you.
I will protect you if you cooperate.

protection_offer.text: You cannot protect me from her resources, Detective. But... I am very tired of being afraid.

choices.text: Then tell me the truth.
What document was she asking you to witness?

threatened_confirm.text: She told me directly. 'One word, Harlow, and I'll ensure it was your hands.' Monstrous woman.

choices.text: Tell me everything.
What happened when you arrived at the manor?

what_document.text: A new will. Harrington was to sign it — transferring the estate fully to her. But when I arrived he was already on the floor. There was blood.

choices.text: You found the body.
She had him killed before you arrived.

found_body.text: He was in the study. The door was open. And she was standing there — perfectly composed. 'This is unfortunate,' she said. 'For both of us.'

choices.text: She implicated you then and there.
Tell me about Doyle.

killed_before.text: By her man Doyle. I had no part in it. I swear it on my licence.

choices.text: Doyle — who is he?
You found the body yourself?

implicated.text: She told me I had called that evening — her word against mine, the family solicitor seen at the scene of death. I had no choice but to keep quiet.

choices.text: Tell me about Doyle.
Will you give a formal statement?

manor_arrival.text: The staff had been dismissed. I should have known — she never does that unless... The door was open. Harrington was dead on the study floor.

choices.text: And Lady Harrington was there.
Who killed him?

fear_probe.text: I am simply a cautious man in a delicate business. Nothing more.

choices.text: A client is threatening you.
You were at the manor Thursday night.

lady_h_question.text: Lady Harrington is a client. I manage the family estate. Entirely routine professional work.

choices.text: She sent for you Thursday night.
When did you last visit the manor?

professional_matter.text: Estate administration. Wills. Trust instruments. Entirely routine.

choices.text: A new will, perhaps?
You seem frightened.

ask_doyle.text: A man Lady Harrington employs for arrangements. He operates from the dockside warehouses — east end, number six quayside. I have seen her write to him.

choices.text: Will you give a formal statement?
Thank you. I have what I need.

about_doyle.text: Muscle for hire. She uses him to make things disappear. Warehouse six, east quay — that's where he operates.

choices.text: Will you testify to what you've told me?
Thank you. I'll find him.

testimony_ask.text: If you can keep me safe from whatever she would do — yes. I will speak to the Inspector. Every detail.

choices.text: You have my word. Good day.

harlow_tells_truth.text: Very well. She summoned me to the manor Thursday. Harrington was already dead when I arrived. Her man Doyle had been there. She threatened to ruin me if I spoke. That is everything.

choices.text: You have done the right thing. Where is Doyle?
Thank you, Harlow.

harlow_breaks.text: Get out. You are going to get us both killed.
